notes.title: Talos: Reawakened Coming April 10 | Play the Demo and Create Unique Puzzles Now
notes.content:
Hi everyone!
It's a glorious day today, as we are ready to announce that [b]The Talos Principle: Reawakened is launching on April 10[/b]. To make the wait easier, the demo version of the game will be available from now until the full launch for your enjoyment.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3398520/The_Talos_Principle_Reawakened_Demo/

This demo gives you a sweet taste of what awaits you in the whole game and allows you to get a glimpse of the world we have rebuilt. More importantly, [b]this demo features the fully featured Puzzle Editor, allowing you to create complete episodes with any number of levels[/b].

[previewyoutube=DQdEC6R-eAY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Re-empowering the modding scene[/h1]

Incredible user-generated content has been the backbone of our games for a long time. Our modding community gave birth to awesome experiences for everyone, and some of the most prominent modders have become integral parts of Croteam over the years.

As we shifted away from our proprietary engine to Unreal while developing The Talos Principle 2, we faced a challenging question: How do we continue empowering our talented community and allowing it to create incredible Talos experiences in the future? The answer was obvious: We only need a powerful built-in tool that removes all technical obstacles and allows our fans to focus on their creativity rather than learning how things work. How hard can it be, right?

In comes the Puzzle Editor. This powerful tool is available to everyone from the main menu and comes with full Workshop support. You can use it to create full episodes with any number of levels, puzzles, and mechanics. You can easily decorate your levels and switch seamlessly between ancient Roman, Egyptian, Medieval, and Alpine settings.

The demo Workshop is fully compatible with the one in the full game, so your efforts in this pre-launch period won't be lost. Create your puzzles and episodes now, then seamlessly transfer them to the main game once it launches on April 10.

[h1]The Elohim Challenge[/h1]

Before you play, allow us to use this opportunity to announce a puzzle-jam community contest, which will start later this week once you’ve had a chance to familiarize yourself with the Puzzle Editor. Everyone will be invited to participate, and we’ll share all the details in a couple of days, so make sure to hang out here or on our Discord to hop right into it once it’s live.

Much love from Croteam!

notes.title: The Talos Principle: A Happy Accident
notes.content:
Some of the best ideas in gaming often come from unexpected places. The Talos Principle is one such story—a critically acclaimed philosophical puzzle game that was never supposed to exist in the first place. What started as an experiment in gameplay mechanics during the development of Serious Sam evolved into an entirely new game that none of the developers had initially planned.

This is the story of how The Talos Principle came to life—born from a simple gameplay idea, fueled by curiosity, and nurtured by a creative team willing to follow where inspiration led them.

[previewyoutube=0qeVxkTrXGQ;full][/previewyoutube]
[h1]Uncover More Behind the Scenes
[/h1]
Experience the full story with exclusive developer commentary, where the creators share insights, challenges, and inspirations behind The Talos Principle. All of this and more await you in The Talos Principle Reawakened. If you're as excited as we are, be sure to add it to your Steam wishlist to stay in the loop and catch the release date reveal very soon.

notes.title: The Philosophy of Reawakening
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33025992/704684bf3181c67dff601204c96ab127c84a00e0.png[/img]

Hi everyone! 
We're a few months away from the launch of [b]The Talos Principle: Reawakened[/b], we'll let you know when that's happening soon enough, so we thought we'd look back at why the game exists in the first place. 

But first, please wishlist the game now if you haven't already.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2806640/The_Talos_Principle_Reawakened/

Remakes and remasters are not rare, but they are certainly not often seen in the indie space. Well, maybe they are in Croteam's little universe ːTheSeriousBombː 

A lot has changed since the original's release, and our team is as passionate as ever. The lingering feeling that there is more to be done with it never disappeared, and it became more prevalent with the launch of The Talos Principle 2.

[h1]A Vision Reconstructed[/h1]

Creating Talos Principle 2 was a long journey. We switched to a new engine, became proficient with various new tools, and finally built the next step in this future history. That enjoyable but frequently challenging process taught us a great deal. 

As the tenth anniversary of the first game approached, and realizing that many new players may be reluctant to return to the original due to it being a decade old, we started to think about all the possibilities that a remaster offered more seriously. We realized focusing on a remaster could bring the game into the same engine as the sequel, upgrade the graphics, fix some quality-of-life issues that had bugged us for years, and introduce the world of Talos to a whole new generation of players in one fell swoop.

So, we decided to proceed! But like anything in life, we didn't want this to be a low-effort product, so we focused on providing tangible value.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Y6MUF1W.gif[/img]

On the technical side, there was far more work than just recreating the levels in Unreal Engine 5. We needed to blend old and new assets to create an up-to-date look. When we re-used the old ones, we put much effort into remastering them thoroughly upgrading meshes and improving textures. 

Most environment assets were remade entirely using texture displacement, which is a perfect match for Nanite because it allows for high-detail geometry. We used many techniques we had learned from developing Talos 2, and in some cases, we improved them even further.

In combination with Unreal's lighting system, which allowed us to create more exaggerated lighting setups, these visual improvements enhanced the simulation's fantastical, hyperreal look. It is a place that is beautiful, eerie, lonely—and won't last forever.

[h1]The Puzzle Evolves[/h1]

On the gameplay side, we introduced a brand new rewind mechanic to allow you to go back between 2 and 10 seconds and fix any missteps. This also helps you avoid being locked in a puzzle without knowing it. This change is based on feedback we received from folks being frustrated when a small mistake meant they had to redo the entire puzzle or situations where players would not be sure if their previous move meant they couldn't proceed.

For similar reasons, we also reworked the infamous time recorder; It now allows you to set up checkpoints (up to 20). You will no longer have to wait in one spot for a prolonged period of time in order to leave the room for later actions, removing the time pressure element. This makes for a more cerebral, less frustrating experience that all our testers describe as a huge improvement. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/2nznts3.gif[/img]

A more minor gameplay tweak, but one that was inspired by the great reception of a similar change in Talos 2, concerns the connectors. It is now possible to deselect connections individually, so you don't have to start from scratch whenever you want to change your configuration.

Finally, we've completely reworked the Messenger hint system, which everyone, including ourselves, found baffling, as the hints were incredibly hard to unlock and not particularly helpful. (Sorry.) Every freed Messenger will now give you three tokens that can be used to skip red sigil puzzles, giving players who are stuck some flexibility - although you still have to earn each Messenger's help!

[h1]A Familiar Future[/h1]

With The Talos Principle: Reawakened, we don't want to change the fundamentals of the experience or transform it into something new. The core gameplay and storytelling principles remain unchanged. However, the game is visually refreshed, with many gameplay frustrations removed, and is now almost ready for its own journey into the future.

There are many more reasons we wanted to create The Talos Principle: Reawakened, including adding new story content and streamlining the user-generated content creation. We'll talk about them in our upcoming blogs, so stay tuned.

Much love, 
Croteam

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6140877/3c009b1cd3f3f3446b46b96941cb34bc296341ab.png[/img]

Hi puzzle lovers,
The Talos Principle 2 is launching this year, and we'll have some big news for you later this week. Exciting, right?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/835960/The_Talos_Principle_2/

To warm you up for playing The Talos Principle 2 soon and the incoming piece of news, we thought we'd warm you up with some reading/watching - 'in case you missed it' style.

First up, why don't you take a look at this great interview from a few months back? Jonas and Verena Kyratzes, gameplay designer Davor Tomicic, and game designer Davor Hunski sat down with Thinky Games during the latest Cerebral Puzzle Showcase and talked what led to TTP2, how it's structured, and what it even is in the first place.

[previewyoutube=B3yoVxhld4Q;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]GAMESCOM 2023[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6140877/5ca6dcc2deba04872c2e02b8e484f4533734f25d.jpg[/img]

We had a great time showing The Talos Principle 2 to press behind closed doors at Gamescom, which led to some really cool previews. Read some cool previews below.

"This optimistic, human-first approach makes The Talos Principle 2 subversive as a work of contemporary sci-fi." - [url=https://www.engadget.com/talos-principle-2-and-the-quiet-subversion-of-optimistic-sci-fi-160014360.html]Engadget[/url]

"If the first game was about what it means to be an individual, the sequel asks what that means for the society that individuals form." - [url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-talos-principle-didnt-need-a-sequel-but-now-that-ive-seen-it-in-action-im-glad-that-its-getting-one/]PC Gamer[/url]

"Talos II aims to continue and deepen the mythology set out in the first game." - [url=https://cogconnected.com/feature/the-talos-principle-ii-preview/]COG Connected[/url]

"The Talos Principle 2 is shaping up to be 2023’s can’t-miss puzzle game" - [url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/the-talos-principle-2-preview-gamescom/]DigitalTrends[/url]

“I'm Ready For The Talos Principle 2 To Put My Brain In A Vice” - [url=https://www.thegamer.com/talos-principle-2-preview-puzzle-changes/]The Gamer[/url]

[h1]CAST REVEAL[/h1]

The Talos Principle 2 is a character-driven exploration of philosophical ideas about faith, technology, history, and the future. We could not have made a game about what it means to be human without these remarkable people.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6140877/bd5c1626e9cc613d4e84b4a07f224515fa5fdb4b.jpg[/img]

Erin Fitzgerald as Alexandra Drennan was the heart and soul of the first game. She returns as [b]Athena[/b], the Founder of New Jerusalem. Because whose voice would she have taken if not Alexandra Drennan's?

[b]Byron [/b]is an optimist, a believer in the humanist ideals of Alexandra Drennan, frustrated by the direction his civilization has been taking. He needed the charm and conviction that the amazing Peter Wingfield brought to the part, which was written for him.

[b]Yaqut [/b]is a young explorer still figuring out his place in the world and struggling with some of the more difficult sides of humanity. We needed someone who could bring real heart, humor and vulnerability to the part, so we wrote it for Adam Green - and got him!

New Jerusalem's Chief Engineer [b]Melville [/b]is a fascinating character, rough around the edges but with a lot going on underneath. She has to grapple with the implications of what you will discover in the Megastructure and Rachel Atkins brought that process to life beautifully.

Byron's best friend [b]Alcatraz [/b]does not share his ideas and worries that humanity will repeat the mistakes of the past. We needed someone who could play this less optimistic perspective with warmth and honesty. It was hard to find the right actor, but Ian Porter blew us away.

[b]Cornelius [/b]is a pivotal figure in the history of New Jerusalem, a figure of great wisdom and emotional depth, and we approached Sean Branney for this part because we were certain he could deliver. He did, in spades.

[b]Miranda [/b]is a mysterious and important character tied to the history of the Megastructure. She sees a great deal of beauty in the world, and we needed someone who could really convey her sense of wonder. Grace Hogg-Robinson was absolutely perfect.

[b]Trevor [/b]was a coworker of Alexandra Drennan's. His recordings give us a different perspective of the events at the Institute for Applied Noematics. Who could play this lovable working-class guy? Only the one it was written for: Joe Lynch.

The man who defined the Talos Principle itself also makes an appearance, and casting [b]Straton of Stageira[/b] was not easy! Until we heard Howard Ward, who captured the voice of a brilliant, complex man who didn't get along terribly well with the philosophers of his own time.

[b]Lifthrasir [/b]is a mysterious, eccentric explorer with a uniquely harsh philosophical perspective. He seems to have preceded you on the island - if you can find them, his recordings may challenge your views on Nature and humanity. David Annen really grasped the character's voice.

And of course it wouldn't be a Talos game without Tim Watson's flawless performance of [b]ELOHIM[/b], whose role in the story is much gentler this time.

This is just a selection of the lovely people who helped us bring robotic humanity alive. We are thankful to all of them and can't wait for you to enjoy their performances when the game launches later this year.

notes.title: The Talos Principle Build 424910 is Live With Tobii Eye Tracking and DX12 Support!
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/LcvmWXP.gif[/img]

Hey everyone! 

It's a happy day today, as The Talos Principle is getting the long-awaited engine upgrade we've been talking about ever since we launched Serious Sam Fusion. This update is very similar to the one we pushed to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/257510/announcements/detail/1773760074713498945]open beta[/url] a few weeks ago, but also fixes most of the things that were reported during beta.

The highlights of the update are [b]Tobii Eye Tracking and DX12 support[/b], as well as further Vulkan tweaks.

[h1]Tobii Eye Tracking[/h1]

We have worked closely with our friends from Tobii to implement exciting eye tracking features like Jam at Gaze, Connect at Gaze and Pick up at Gaze. Those features allow you to be more efficient in your problem-solving adventures, while the Extended View feature and Clean UI improve your immersion in Talos' world of puzzles and philosophy.

To celebrate this launch Tobii is about to have a cool contest, so be sure to jump on their [url=https://twitter.com/tobiigaming]Twitter[/url] page, give them a follow and await further instructions.


If you are having issues please report by starting a new thread in the tech support forum [https://steamcommunity.com/app/257510/discussions/1/] and we'll be on it straight away.

As always, if you are not satisfied with this build there's an option to go back to the older one. To do so, please follow the steps below:

— right click on The Talos Principle in your Steam library
— go to properties > betas
— opt-in by picking the "previousversion" branch in the drop-down menu



For all things Croteam, chatter or all-around fun stuff, we're always available on [url=http://www.facebook.com/croteam]Facebook[/url], [url=http://www.twittter.com/croteam]Twitter[/url] and [url=http://www.discord.gg/croteam]Discord[/url]. Hit us up!

notes.title: The Talos Principle update 326589 is live!
notes.content:

- Fixed some rendering issues under OpenGL graphics API.
- Better detection of usable CPU cores.
- Fixed problems with Chinese Traditional translation in Road to Gehenna.
- Removed usage of D3DX library DLL.
- Enlarged FPS graph and added average line.
- Fixed problem with imprecise frame-rate limitation on Windows platforms.

If you experience serious issues after the update, you may switch to the "previousversion" branch.
Here's how:
- locate the game in the Steam's "Library" panel
- right click and invoke "Properties"
- select the "Betas" tab
- choose "previousversion"

notes.title: The Talos Principle: Road to Gehenna DLC announced!!!
notes.content:
[h1]The Talos Principle DLC announced[/h1]
Your favourite brain-taxing puzzler The Talos Principle is getting an expansion, called the Road to Gehenna. It will cast you as Elohim's messenger, and will send you through a new, previously hidden chunk of the simulation. Fun fact: Gehenna has all manner of religious significance, and could also theoretically contain lasers you can redirect.

[h1]Road to Gehenna[/h1]
With a four-episode add-on, Croteam is promising the most advanced and challenging puzzles yet made for the game. It'll also feature new story from the main game's writers, Tom Jubert and Jonas Kyratzes.

"We wanted to revisit the world of The Talos Principle and deliver new characters and a new world with its own history and culture,” said Jubert. “With Road to Gehenna we have created an all-new narrative which both branches off from and expands the original character’s journey."

The Talos Principle: Road to Gehenna is due out this Spring.

http://www.croteam.com/the-talos-principle-road-to-gehenna-dlc-announcement/

- Fixed a rare crash that would sometimes happen when trying to show a system message on Linux.
- Fixed a crash which was preventing safe mode from working on Linux and OSX.
- Fixed an issue preventing system messages from being shown if running the game in fullscreen on OSX.

notes.title: The Talos Principle - Update 222477
notes.content:
Build 222477 for The Talos Principle is released. 
If you have previously opted into public beta, you already have this.

Here are the changes:

New features:
- Upon collecting all main story sigils, a backup of your progress is created which is never overwritten. This makes it easy and safe to try out different endings.
- Text files no longer require signed credentials. In other words: .lua, .xml, .txt and any other text files can now freely be created/modified by any external tools, even for the non-moddable version of the game.
- Added motion sickness menu.
- Added 'Fast Forward' command which causes in-game time to pass at an accelerated rate. By default, this command has no binding.
- Added hints for using puzzle arrangers.
- Benchmark can now be used in the full game without completing the demo episode.
- Added alternate version of soundtrack without Elohim voiceovers.
- Jammer shenanigans will now be interrupted via Developer Intervention(TM).

Bug fixes:
- Fixed several rare crashes that would sometimes randomly occur during gameplay.
- Cheats now persist between level changes.
- Fixed an issue with time recording mechanic preventing the correct solution of 'A Ditch and a Fence' puzzle from working at poor framerates.
- Fixed an exploit on 'Oubliette' puzzle allowing it to be solved without using time recording mechanic.
- Launching the game in safe mode no longer overwrites all previous settings, but merely supplants them temporarily.
- Fixed an issue where Steam avatar images would sometimes not be visible on tombstones under OpenGL.
- Fixed issues with water rippler and shadow rendering on certain multi-GPU setups.
- Fixed an issue with erroneous model culling on ultra-wide screen setups.
- Fixed a rare crash that could happen during OpenGL initialization on certain systems.
- Fixed a rare crash when changing sound devices.
- Fixed a memory leak when editing meshes or painting textures in the Editor.
- Fixed a rare crash when exporting animations from the Editor via FBX.
- World scene selection was unintentionally unavailable in Editor scripting. Fixed.
- Error messages will no longer pop up if the game is played in Big Picture mode.
- Improved timings on QR painting animation to better match the appearing of the painted QR code.
- Upon saving player profile, a backup of the existing profile is first created (with added .bkp extension), before overwriting it. This should prevent data loss in case of disk errors or crashes during profile saving.
- Several fixes and improvements on the autotest bot.
- Significantly improved Polish translation.
- Several localization improvements for all languages.

Optimizations:
- Improved LODs on many models.
- Optimized memory usage and performance of water rendering and made visual improvements (e.g., water ripples now bounce off surface edges).
- Optimized tombstone and computer terminal screen rendering.
- Several fixes and performance improvements in the OpenGL renderer.
- Improved appearance of turret lasers for players with disabled MSAA.

Linux/OSX:
- Added support for additional gamepads on Linux.
- Added support for DualShock 4 controller on OSX.
- Fixed an issue with copy&pasting on Linux.

notes.title: The Talos Principle - Update 220675
notes.content:
Build 220675 for The Talos Principle is now live on Steam. This is the same as last "publicbeta", with a small addition of a fix for a blocker bug caused by localization on some languages.

Here are the changes since the last version:

Language fixes:
- Elevator control codes were generated wrong in Spanish, Italian and Croatian, causing inability to unlock some floors.
- Game now properly detects change in Steam language and resets user selected language.
- Language menu screen is now updated with correctly translated language names once desired language is changed. 
- Terminal dialogs were sometimes in wrong language if language was changed without restarting the entire game. Fixed.
- Improved translations for Spanish, Polish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese.

General fixes:
- Terminals were unusable if HUD was disabled. Fixed.
- Grass/pebbles were sometimes not immediately recached when (re)loading a level, causing visual pops within a few seconds. Fixed.
- Tentative fix for a rare crash when creating window on start on some machines.
- Tentative fix for rare crash when opening texts in terminals.
- Fixed a rare crash that happened if you held a key pressed during loading of an ending cutscene.
- Fixed some models disappearing too early on Lowest.

Misc fixes:
- Fixed occasional performance stutter when rotating view on B2.
- Fixed a hole on Abode C.
- Fixed shadows on Prototype Roman Villa.
- Added a secret star on Prototype Roman Villa.
- Fixed various small visual/functional issues on several Easter eggs (details not provided for spoiler prevention).
- Fixed visibility issue in 3rd person on C1.а
- Fixed cliff-terrain hole on B3.
- Added a wire for visual hinting that was missing on "Big Stairs, Little Stairs" (C3).
- Fixed missing collision on some decorative support models on the "boss puzzle".
- Fixed wrong placement of grass on A4.
- Fixed visual issues on A1, including wrong shadows on Lowest settings, visibility in 3rd person and others.
- Fixed some light/shadow issues on Lowest settings on the Nexus.
- Fixed a rare crash in Redeem Rewards menu.
- Fixes for frame rate sometimes stuttering a bit during background loading.
- Fixed HUD on some Easter eggs not showing correctly if MaxMPix is not unlimited.
- Fixed problem with dynamic shadows not rendered when changing to/from prebaked lights mode in menu when there's a level in the background. 

- Editor: Fixed several cases where vertex move tool was working wrong.
- Prototype DLC: Prototype puzzles now use the old prototype versions of Jammers, Connectors and Mines.
- Prototype DLC: Fixed a broken fan setup on one puzzle.

notes.title: Welcome to The Talos Principle
notes.content:
Welcome to The Talos Principle. Thanks for your interest in the game. Allow us to give you a overview of the things that are going on in our community. First little bit about the game.


[h1]The Talos Principle[/h1]
The Talos Principle is a first-person puzzle game in the tradition of philosophical science fiction. Made by Croteam, the creators of Serious Sam, and written by Tom Jubert (FTL, The Swapper) and Jonas Kyratzes (The Sea Will Claim Everything).

Release trailer:
http://youtu.be/m8oxVPeTUnU
Check game reviews on [url=http://www.metacritic.com/game/pc/the-talos-principle?recent-sort=metascore]Metacritic[/url] or read short reviews overview [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/257510/discussions/0/626329186711175876/]here[/url].


[h1]The Talos Principle Public Test[/h1]
The Public Test for The Talos Principle consists of four increasingly difficult complete puzzle levels, where players will be able to test the range of puzzle mechanics, as well as run a benchmarking AI bot for their PC. 

The Public Test is meant to serve as additional stress and compatibility testing. So feel free to try before you buy. If Public Test works well on your machine full game will work well too.

http://store.steampowered.com/app/330710


[h1]The Talos Principle Community[/h1]
We plan to support [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/257510]The Talos Principle Steam Community hub[/url] as a major spot for providing news about the game, announcing future content and updates, broadcasting major happenings in community and workshop, and listening to the Vox Populi (that means you) in Discussions. If you have any troubles with a game here is the best way to let us know and we will react as soon as possible. This is probably the best way to follow developments on The Talos Principle on your PC, since you are already logged into Steam and all actions are only a click away.

[url=https://www.facebook.com/TheTalosPrinciple]The Talos Principle official Facebook page[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/TalosPrinciple]The Talos Principle official Twitter page[/url] are the best way to follow game on the go, using mobile devices. Expect to find all relevant news and developments regarding The Talos Principle game. Also if you are intrigued by scientific and philosophical themes touched in The Talos Principle and you want more in-depth view into those matters, from new developments in science and philosophy to relevant games, movies and books about those themes, social networks are the best places to follow.

notes.title: The Talos Principle Themed Craft Contest! Your chance to win free copy of The Talos Principle!
notes.content:
[h1]WHAT IS IT?[/h1]

With the impending release of The Talos Principle in less than one month, we’re giving another opportunity for you to increase your chances to win a free copy of The Talos Principle. We want to spark the creativity within our community and see what ideas unfold.

This contest is organized by community members, for community members. We will be giving away two free copies of The Talos Principle to the best entries just in time for the game’s launch. We understand it can be difficult to come up with ideas for a game that is not yet released, but you can also use this as an opportunity to be as creative as you’d like. In addition to the Talos Principle Public Test and Sigils of Elohim, you may consider looking at the following promotional materials for inspiration:

[url=http://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2014/10/30/the-talos-principle-preview/]RockPaperShotgun’s The Talos Principle Preview[/url]
[url=http://www.unitedfrontgaming.com/pc/post/2633/ufg-goes-hands-on-with-the-talos-principal]UnitedFrontGaming’s Hands on with The Talos Principle[/url]
[url=http://www.hardcoregamer.com/2014/11/05/confusion-the-talos-principles-biggest-tool/115519/]HardcoreGamer’s Confusion: The Talos Principles Biggest Tool[/url]
[url=http://www.gamefront.com/the-talos-principle-preview-existential-crises/]GameFront’s The Talos Principle Preview[/url]
[url=http://canadianonlinegamers.com/preview/the-talos-principle-hands-on-preview-philosophical-puzzle-game-with-some-fantastic-level-design/]CanadianOnlineGamer’s The Talos Principle Hands On[/url]
[url=http://www.everybodyplays.co.uk/news/PS4/The-Talos-Principle-Hands-On-Preview-Playing-with-lasers/1769]EverybodyPlays’ The Talos Principle Hands On[/url]


[h1]WHAT MEDIUMS CAN I USE?[/h1]

Anything! The last thing we want to do is limit your creativity. You have a cool visual, audible, or literary medium idea? We would love to see it! Here are just a few ideas:
[list]
[*]Photoshop edits
[*]Hand drawn art
[*]Live Photoshoots
[*]Custom Birthday Cake
[*]LEGO Model
[*]Original short story or poem
[*]Original / remixed music
[/list]


[h1]HOW DO I ENTER?[/h1]

There are just three simple steps to enter and have your chance at winning a free copy:

[olist]
[*]Submit your entry to any free hosting service (imgur, photobucket, pastebin, etc etc).
[*]Reply to [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/257510/discussions/0/624075036337951389/)]this thread[/url] with a link to your entry 
[*]Type a short explanation of your work and what you look forward to most in The Talos Principle.
[/olist]

That’s it! You may submit as many creations as you like to improve your chances of winning!


[h1]RULES[/h1]

[olist]
[*]You must be the author/creator of any work submitted to the contest. You may not edit a previous submission without prior written consent from the original author.
[*]Your submission must fall within Steam’s guidelines (See: https://support.steampowered.com/kb_article.php?ref=4045-USHJ-3810)
[*]Your entry must have some relation to The Talos Principle (gameplay mechanics, environments, characters, etc). However, your creation can be as unique as you like and can even speculate regarding unannounced game features.
[*]We reserve the right to disqualify any submissions that break any of the above rules.
[*]By submitting your creation(s), you grant permission to the contest moderators and/or Croteam to post your material in promotion advertisements and/or to showcase entry submissions.


[h1]DEADLINES[/h1]

Please reply to this thread with your entry by Friday, December 5th, 6:00 pm GMT. Winners will be announced on the following Tuesday, December 9th, 6:00 pm GMT.


[h1]PRIZES[/h1]

Each submitted entry will be ranked by a small panel of judges (including a few Croteam developers) in categories of creativity (i.e. originality) and execution (i.e. professionalism). The top pick for both categories will win a free copy of The Talos Principle. Good luck!

notes.title: The Talos Principle Public Test gets updated! Try it now!
notes.content:
If you missed the news yesterday, we released The Talos Principle Public Test to serve as additional stress and compatibility testing before The Talos Principle launches later this year. 

Playing The Talos Principle Public Test day one was smooth experience for most players, but some encountered certain issues. We adressed and fixed all major issues in the meantime so now we released updated and more stabile version!

The Talos Principle Public Test will give you good taste of the game itself, so feel free to check it out! It is free after all ;)
Find and install The Talos Principle Public Test here: http://store.steampowered.com/app/330710/

The Talos Principle Public Test - Build 216187 changelog:
[list]
[*]Windows: Fixed problem with crashing, black screen or garbled display after Alt-Tab under Direct3D 11.
[*]OSX: Fixed problem with black objects on some OS X machines.
[*]Option for slower player walking speed in Options>Game Options menu.
[*]More varied music.
[*]For high-DPI mice, enabled lower mouse sensitivity in Options>Controls>Keyboard and Mouse menu.
[*]Fixed benchmark not enabling if game was quit after finishing it.
[*]Linux: Logitech F710 and F310 gamepads are now supported on Linux.
[*]Fixed visibility problem on the windowed wall outside Medium puzzle.
[*]Fixed some vegetation that was below the terrain.
[*]Fixed collision on some direction signs.
[*]Added more detail to gates in the cathedral.
[*]Various small fixes and adjustments in the level.
[/list]
